title: AI infrastructure financing boom raises risk of private credit bubble: 8090 CEO Chamath Palihapitiya
key_facts: Chamath Palihapitiya, CEO of 8090 and Social Capital, posted on X that AI is increasingly funded by debt.
He cited a $35 billion Apollo and Blackstone vehicle in Q2 2026 to buy chips and lease them to Anthropic.
UBS described it as the largest private credit deal on record, per his post.
Direct lenders made about $23 billion of loans to private-equity-backed US companies that quarter.
S&P Global forecasts about $870 billion of 2026 spending by Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle and SpaceX (xAI).
The Bank for International Settlements found AI-related private loans carried a 6.2-point spread against 6.1 for other loans.
He said the market is already distinguishing among deals.
quote_evidence: "The AI buildout is increasingly funded by debt, and private credit is playing a much bigger role than it did even a year ago," he wrote.
That narrow difference could mean "lenders are underestimating AI-related risks, equity investors are overestimating future profits, or both", Palihapitiya said.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent investor argues lenders are not charging enough extra for AI risk.
